# Eric Rash context brief (for staff-development and department-building recommendations)

Compiled 2026-09-24 from the DEV workspace, the SecondBrain vault, and Claude memory. Read-only pass; nothing else was modified. Sources are date-stamped in section 8 because they span June to September 2026 and some are stale. Anything not stated in a source is marked (inferred). No athlete names or athlete health information appear here by design.

Naming rule for anything staff-facing that comes out of this: Athletic Performance (not S&C), Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science).

## Role and remit

- Title: Director of Applied Performance, Baylor University Athletics. About eight years in the department, promoted into the director seat from within. Source: `ContextVault/Career-Context-Document.md` (2026-06-08).
- Where the unit sits: Applied Performance is a support and enablement function inside Health & Wellness, behind the athlete-facing units (Athletic Medicine, Athletic Performance, Mental Health, Performance Nutrition). It is not athlete-facing itself. Source: Career-Context-Document; `Education_Alignment_Initiative/docs/context.md`.
- Reporting line: formal supervisor is Chris Ruf, Director of Athletic Performance, since a 2025 reporting change that moved Eric off administrative senior staff (where he reported to Kenny Boyd, Executive Senior Associate AD). The June career document records that the change cost him access to Kenny and senior conversations. Since then: the July 2026 responsibilities document came from Chris and Kenny jointly, the biweekly status report goes to both, and in August Kenny named Eric the Athletics point of contact to ITS. Some access to Kenny has been rebuilt through the JD process and the technology work (inferred). Chris prefers email. Sources: Career-Context-Document; `KeystoneOS memory project-jd-okr-2026.md`; `SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/docs/MICAH_MEETING_REQUEST_2026-08-13.md`; `BAIR_Steering_Committee/docs/context.md` (which lists Kenny as the person Eric reports to; treat as the BAIR-lane relationship, not the formal line).
- The July 2026 JD shifted the role from doer to director. It names: department oversight, BAIR Steering Committee oversight and organization, HPI (human performance integration) protocols, technology vetting, vendor relations and onboarding, data infrastructure, guidance to Health & Wellness staff on technology and data, and Spirit Squad as a direct team-training responsibility. Source: `project-jd-okr-2026.md`; `SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-JD-2026/decisions.md` (2026-07-17).
- Three permanent service pillars in the current OKR structure (v3): Data Systems & Analytics, Education, Research & Development, plus an enabling objective, Leadership & Visibility. Mission sentence used in briefings: "Applied Performance turns Baylor's athlete data into decisions that keep athletes available and performing." North star: be the best applied performance department in the country. Source: `SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3, Fall set authored 2026-09-14).
- Eric's protected hands-on lanes (not delegated): HPI protocol and its dashboarding; technology vetting; white-paper analysis; one-off reports and dashboards for sports. Delegation stops at those boundaries. Source: OKR doc v3.
- Decision rights (June 2026 read): owns what projects to pursue, what questions to chase, how to source data, and can take a meeting with almost anyone on campus. Needs Chris for spending and hiring. No budget line. No control over whether other units adopt his work. The JD clarifying questions (July) show that authority thresholds, budget, evaluation of staff, and escalation were still undefined at that point. Sources: Career-Context-Document; `SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-JD-2026/JD-clarifying-questions.md`.
- Accountability: Eric authors his own OKRs; no one external holds him to them. The v3 system adds self-imposed teeth: semester cycles, an Oct 15 mid-semester checkpoint, a Dec 18 close, and a timer-checked project slate. Source: OKR doc v3; `SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-Operating-Cadence.md` (2026-09-14).

## Staff and structure

Applied Performance unit (as of the v3 OKR doc and the 2026-08-24 supervisor update):

- Eric Rash, Director. Presents solo in briefings; staff appear on the org and lanes slide.
- AJ Tademy, Applied Performance Specialist, Football. Full-time. Owns football day-to-day: fall-camp planning, the practice-load framework (FaceComps color-coded day system and rep-count load model), the plan-vs-actual review to the football staff, and all football staff communications. JD relationship verb: Oversee. Concretely that means a weekly 1:1, Eric reviews any artifact before it leaves the department, and Eric stays out of daily operations. Summer KR 4.2 (AJ full handoff through fall camp) scored 1.0, so the handoff worked. Strength on record: ready to run the lane; the framework was jointly presented to staff before handoff. Gap: none stated in sources. Sources: OKR doc v3; `decisions.md` 0004; `JD-2026/CONTEXT.md`.
- Noah, Basketball Applied Performance GA. JD relationship verb: Support and guide (mentoring-weighted oversight; Eric teaches procedures, policies and data-management practice; Noah executes "with training wheels on"; Eric remains accountable for outcomes). Summer KR 4.3 (onboarding checklist plus weekly 1:1) scored 0.0. Fall KR 4.2 is a Noah 1:1 every two weeks. Open question to Chris: whether the basketball position is permanent, renewable, or disappears when the GA term ends. Sources: OKR doc v3; CONTEXT.md; JD-clarifying-questions.
- Linda. Role under Applied Performance is still being defined. Leadership stated Eric's role toward her is supportive, not directive. Eric met with her twice in August and they listed four potential projects supporting Tennis and Athletic Performance. A `DEV/Linda Projects` folder exists. Sources: `Supervisor_Reviews/updates/Bi-Weekly_Update_2026-08-24.md`; decisions.md 0003; DEV `CLAUDE.md` and `PROGRAM.md`.
- Blake Wright, PhD fellow, has left the organization (established 2026-07-17). He is removed from all forward planning; his KR co-ownership was redistributed to Eric and AJ; the white paper is now Eric's sole critical path with Blake credited as co-author. Several older sources still list him as current (the Applied-Performance-Hub dated 2026-06-01, the BAIR context, the okr-staff-meeting-prep memory). Treat those as stale. Source: decisions.md 0003 and 0005.
- Student workers: the 08-24 update says "whatever student workers we have." No names, count, or scope anywhere in the sources.
- Interns: an intern program exists as a concept with a curriculum design and SOP templates, but there is no evidence in the sources of a current intern cohort. See section 3.

Adjacent groups and named contacts (staff only):

- Chris Ruf, Director of Athletic Performance, formal supervisor. Values communication, follow-through, order, high execution. Gives little direction; has not articulated a vision (June read). Prefers email.
- Kenny Boyd, Executive Senior Associate AD. Chairs the technology and software review group. Reviewer on policy and framework drafts with firm editorial preferences (section 6). Prefers quick visual scanning over dense documents.
- Athletic Medicine: Joe Smith (AT, receiver of the return-to-performance course); Jacob (approves the course; role not stated, likely Athletic Medicine leadership, inferred); Jeremy Frazier (staff physical therapist, PI on a BAIR cohort proposal). The RTP Working Group spans Health & Wellness and produced a gaps overview for Kenny.
- Research: Dr. Andrew Gallucci (research team lead, central to BAIR framework and review; receiver of the women's health survey data set); Dr. Sarah Snitker (Robbins College collaborator).
- Student Services leadership (receivers of the Fall education KR): Kenny Boyd, Chris Ruf, Carrie, Josh Young, Kevin Washington, Kristen Fant.
- Business Office and marketing: Cody Hall (Athletics Business Office; AI "guinea pig" for content workflows; website partner for the education hub); Erin Boyette (Business Office); Jovon Overshown (Athletics). Kenny asked Eric to report out to Cody, Jovon and Kenny after each ITS meeting.
- ITS: Micah Lamb (director-level contact; writing a counter-proposal to the tech framework); Jon Allen (ITS; key reviewer on tech deployments and data policy). Lisa Creed (campus partner coordination).
- Volleyball: Mike Wenger and Ryan McGuyre use the Kinexon-based dashboard weekly (the one fully adopted sport-facing deliverable outside football).
- AP Clinic: Courteney Tompkins owns the event; Eric assists at her direction (JD verb: Assist).
- Doug McNamee, senior leadership, named as a visibility target for BAIR.
- External data-governance advisers: Anthony (formal proposal owed), Jonathan (AI Risk Navigator, vendor risk), Lisa (campus partner coordination).

Reporting lines summary: Eric reports to Chris; Chris sits under Kenny. AJ and Noah are overseen by Eric, but whether Eric has input on their hiring, reviews and corrective conversations was an open question to Chris as of July. Linda is supported, not directed. Sources: JD-clarifying-questions; CONTEXT.md.

Sport coverage baseline (2026-09-14): named in a project or OKR: Football (via AJ) and Volleyball (direct). Meeting-corpus evidence also shows Baseball, Softball, Acrobatics & Tumbling, Tennis, Women's Golf. Zero evidence for either basketball program, Soccer, Track and XC, Equestrian, Men's Golf. Basketball is described as self-contained and resistant to involvement. The RTP lane (24 meetings) and StaffMeet (29) dwarf any single sport but appear in no planning document. Source: `SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md`.

## Active projects and initiatives

Fall 2026 slate (cap 5, timer-checked, each with a charter in `DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json`):

- Tech_Inventory_Analysis (Fall KR 1.1, receiver Kenny Boyd, finish 2026-10-09). Survey closed with 52 responses, 32 of 32 units answering for themselves, 188 distinct products, 75 likely touching athlete data, 123 single-unit products, 9 retired. One-page exec summary and findings report build from clean CSVs. Final run after 29 September. The timer shows the "plan agreed with receiver" step (due 09-18) overdue as of today. Source: `Tech_Inventory_Analysis/docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-16.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, memory `project_tech-inventory-refresh.md`; `portfolio.py slate-check` run 2026-09-24.
- HPI_Protocol v1 (Fall KR 1.2, receivers Chris Ruf and Kenny Boyd, finish 2026-12-11). Data integration, flow, storage, dashboarding, interpretation. Summer KR scored 0.0; plan-agreed step due 10-01. Whether HPI is a Baylor-defined framework or an implementation of an existing model was an open question to Kenny in July. Source: OKR doc v3; JD-clarifying-questions. No DEV repo found for it; `RTP_WorkingGroup/HPI_DataDepot.xlsx` exists.
- Education_Curriculum (Fall KR 2.1, receivers Student Services leadership, finish 2026-12-11). Four education pieces (slide decks or short videos) built from strength-coach interviews. Plan-agreed step due 09-25. Education scored 0.03 in Summer and was 0-for-3 for the second cycle running; the diagnosed blocker was launch (open-ended sign-off loop, distribution re-planned around an unlaunched website). Reset rule: advance notice, not approval-seeking; email now, website later. Source: OKR doc v3; decisions.md 0006.
- RTP_Constraints_Course (Fall KR 2.2, receiver Joe Smith, approval by Jacob, finish 2026-12-11). Six-lesson constraints-led return-to-performance course; Joe runs one real session with it. Book ingest done, lesson 0002 next. Plan-agreed step due 09-24. Source: memory `project_rtp-cla-course.md`; `PROGRAM.md`.
- WomensHealth_Survey (Fall KR 3.1, receiver Andrew Gallucci, finish 2026-12-11). Clean the survey data set with a data dictionary and hand it over. Plan-agreed step due 09-25. Source: OKR doc v3; Active-Projects.
- Next up (Spring unless a slot opens): NCAA_BestPractices_Doc for Chris Ruf, which is also where the data-continuity plan and the tech decision matrix sign-off were folded. Repo exists and is empty. Source: OKR doc v3; `NCAA_BestPractices_Doc/docs/STATUS.md`.

Other live or recently shipped work:

- SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework (Athletics software and technology management framework). Shipped set dated 2026-08-14: framework with NCAA performance-technology crosswalk, workflow, exec summary, two intake forms, request tracker. Reviewed 2026-08-13 by Kenny's group with ITS. Outcome: ITS (Micah) wants a standardized intake, not a parallel process; convergence on a one-page checklist; Eric drafted a three-question routing sheet (Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive; Business Office first). Known gaps not yet written: education section, working group definition, transfer student-athlete handling, consent template, annual survey. Blocked on the ITS intake path. Parked as a project; the ITS thread continues inside Tech_Inventory_Analysis. Sources: `SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/docs/MEETING_RECORD_2026-08-13_tech-software-review.md`, `ROUTING_ONEPAGER_ATH_2026-08-13.md`, memory `project_ath-tech-framework.md`.
- Weekly_Research_Review ("Research in 5"). Pipeline built 2026-09-16: one paper becomes a five-slide deck (dark and light), a Teams post, and a staff email, with a citation verifier. #001 (v4) ready to send; #002 (v2) verified and cleared 2026-09-21. Audience is deliberately mixed: Athletic Performance, Athletic Medicine, nutrition, mental health, Applied Performance, sport coaches, admin. Open: whether Teams keeps markdown formatting; who is on the training-staff email list; whether the three-slide "readout" format (names an owner and a decision) becomes standard. Source: `Weekly_Research_Review/docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`.
- Education_Alignment_Initiative (EAI). Framework at capstone stage: Strategic Alignment Framework, Performance Education Strategic Plan, EAI Integration Guide, an "Education Czar" proposal (a coordination function, not a position, bridging Student Services and Health & Wellness), Performance School (staff) and Performance Academy (athletes), a 45-topic "5 Slides in 5 Minutes" pipeline across 8 domains. Thirteen documents migrated to `docs/program/` on 2026-09-11. No delivery evidence beyond the documents; the staff deck series produced three decks and stopped. Source: `Education_Alignment_Initiative/docs/context.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/program/Education_Czar_Proposal_v2.md`; `CPSS_BaylorSportScience_Curriculum/README.md`.
- Intern_Curriculum and CPSS_BaylorSportScience_Curriculum. Module-based internship curriculum designed outside the academic calendar: eleven modules in four blocks, an intern-facing handbook, NSCA CPSS text as the content spine (not exam prep). Draft v1 2026-08-18; chapter assignments proposed, not signed off. Design rule to preserve: a module is not a PowerPoint Eric builds; the intern reads and does the task, Eric's cost is twenty minutes of discussion; slides accumulate only after the same explanation recurs. The Intern_Curriculum repo holds only a Clemson sample zip; the Baylor curriculum content lives in the CPSS repo. Source: `CPSS_BaylorSportScience_Curriculum/README.md`; `Intern_Curriculum/docs/context.md`.
- Performance_Playbook. Departmental user manual: a two-column Word SOP template covering the technology lifecycle, a Baylor-branded PowerPoint template structured as a 16-week curriculum (technical plus soft skills), and a technology SOP template. Baylor Applied Performance Playbook PDF exists. Source: `Performance_Playbook/docs/context.md`, `docs/program/Technology_SOP_Template.md`.
- Department_Audits. A complete "Comprehensive Sport Performance Departmental Audit" playbook (Capacity vs Impact lens, six domains including Technology & Data Ecosystem, instruments synthesized inside the .docx: pre-audit questionnaire, staff interview guide, athlete survey, training observation checklist, scorecard, impact vs effort matrix). Written generically under a "Collegiate Performance Solutions" byline, not yet run at Baylor. Three non-negotiables it states: athlete-centered and coach-driven, evidence over tradition, administrator-backed. Source: `Department_Audits/Comprehensive_Departmental_Audit_Plan_v2.docx`, `docs/context.md`.
- BAIR Steering Committee (Baylor applied research arm). Framework in force is the January 2026 revision: feasibility gate plus five weighted dimensions (Strategic Alignment 31, Athlete & Staff Burden 26, Revenue & Resources 20, Research Quality 15, Gender Equity 10). Oversight runs by email; MS Teams and Planner are its home. Summer KR "committee organized, first meeting scheduled" scored 0.2 and is parked. One proposal still under review. Source: `BAIR_Steering_Committee/docs/context.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`.
- RTP Working Group (Health & Wellness, 2025-26). Gaps overview prepared for Kenny names four areas: programming the process, medical admin, intake and assessment, staff education and skill. Staff-education gaps named: onboarding under regular turnover, technical plus "coach's eye" education, teaching skill. Proposed solutions: a manual for new hires, a presentation series for staff, movement-skill workshops. Force-plate RTP progress reports exist as a template. Source: `global-memory/dev-docs/RTP_WorkingGroup/program/rtp-gaps-overview-for-kb.md`; `RTP_WorkingGroup/docs/STATUS.md`; `PERFORMANCE.md`.
- Program_Context_Meet. A designed 20-minute, one-on-one, non-evaluative conversation with each lead performance coach producing a descriptive profile, feedback on Applied Performance support, and 60 to 90 day actions. Guide written 2026-07-27; no evidence the conversations have run. Source: `Program_Context_Meet/PROJECT_LOG.md`.
- Administrative stakeholder briefing ("Briefing Asset"). Three pillars plus capability menu plus one-page leave-behind with an owner on every line; v1 deployment to administrators and sport administrators in an existing admin meeting; deck v1 was due 2026-08-14 and the 08-24 update asked Kenny and Chris for time at an SPA meeting. No evidence it has been delivered. Source: `SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-Stakeholder-Briefing-Plan.md`; 08-24 update.
- Sport_Tech_Vetting. Technology decision matrix (STRN quality framework, assessment sheet). Summer KR "adopted as standard vendor intake with Chris's written sign-off" scored 0.3 and was folded into the NCAA best practices doc. Paused. Source: OKR doc v3; `Sport_Tech_Vetting/docs/STATUS.md`.
- AI integration initiative (May 2026). Two threads: Claude workflow automation for content and admin work (skills for agendas and branded decks, an internal AI usage survey, enterprise licenses, a mid-June staff PD session; Cody Hall as pilot user) and a Databricks/Player360 data platform evaluation. Friction named: institutional IT policy and generational resistance. No outcome recorded after June. Source: memory `project_ai-integration-initiative.md`; Applied-Performance-Hub (2026-06-01).
- Athlete data governance (May 2026). Phased governance and compliance framework with an external advisory firm (discovery, policies and SOPs, vendor risk assessments, training; 50-plus vendors; FERPA, HIPAA, NCAA). Waiting on Anthony's formal proposal since May. Source: memory `project_athlete-data-governance.md`.
- Transformative_Athlete_Experience. Proposal brief (HTML and PDF) exists; parked. Source: `Transformative_Athlete_Experience/docs/STATUS.md`.

- White paper (converted from a short report) and research repository MVP: both scored near zero in Summer and are parked to the OKR parking lot. Source: OKR doc v3.
- Sport-facing data systems that Eric or AJ run (VALD ForceDecks monitoring workbook, GPS load reporting, Kinexon volleyball, CMJ dashboard, S2 cognition reports, CATES evaluation framework, injury surveillance at program level). These are the pipelines the pillars sit on; several are single-person builds. Source: `PERFORMANCE.md`.

Summer 2026 scorecard for calibration: all 14 KRs averaged 0.23. Data Systems 0.43, Education 0.03, Research & Development 0.13, Leadership & Visibility 0.33. Two KRs fully met: per-sport dashboards in weekly use (Volleyball direct, Football via AJ) and the AJ fall-camp handoff. Everything that needed Eric to start and finish a document scored near zero. Source: OKR doc v3, Aug 31 review scored 2026-09-14.

## Existing forums and vehicles

Verified as running or built:

- Biweekly status report to Chris Ruf and Kenny Boyd (Fall KR 4.1). Five headings: Shipped / In Progress / Decisions Needed / Risks and No-Surprises / Next Two Weeks, under 300 words, email. First one sent 2026-08-24. Built by the `status-report` skill from a nightly supervisor log (`interview-me` Part 0) plus the ledger and registry; the memory notes that roughly two thirds of what belongs in the report appears in no automated source. Status of report #2 (due 09-18): not on disk in `Supervisor_Reviews/updates` or Drive; the slate timer reports the 09-18 checkpoint overdue; working memory says "#3 by 9/25". Built 2026-06-04 for the first unit OKR check-in with AJ and Blake; reusable as a template. The weekly Thursday check-in it supported is retired ("it needed Blake"). Source: memory `reference_okr-staff-meeting-prep.md`; Operating-Cadence.

- SOP and curriculum templates (Performance_Playbook), intern module list and handbook (CPSS repo), audit playbook (Department_Audits).

Announced or planned, not verified in the sources:

- Applied Performance staff meetings every other week (Noah, Basketball, AJ, Linda, student workers), announced in the 08-24 update. No agenda, minutes, or later mention found.

1	# What this material is
     2	
     3	"Running The Room" is a paid online course from Old Bull Performance, written and presented by Dr Jason Weber (former AFL high-performance manager, creator of the SpeedSig gait product). It is for people who lead or want to lead a high-performance department. The material is 31 lessons (webinars, short video labs, three podcasts) and 26 PDFs (blogs, cheat sheets, worksheets, workbooks) across four modules. The course files label the fourth block "Module 6"; the Drive folder and these notes call it Module 4.
     4	
     5	The argument in one sentence: departments buy technology faster than they build the people, language and procedures needed to turn it into decisions, and the fix is discipline written down.
     6	
     7	## The four modules
     8	
     9	- **Module 1, People, language and discipline before technology.** Audit staff on a knowledge and behaviour grid, agree a common language (means before modality before technology), and inventory the tech stack by what it measures, not by brand.
    10	- **Module 2, Turning technology into defensible decisions.** Separate measurement from inference, map every tool to a question and an owner, decide whether a metric is monitored or tested, pre-agree decision gates, and quantify noise so the gates hold.
    11	- **Module 3, Discipline equals freedom.** Meeting problems are meeting-type problems: name the modality (Decide, Diagnose, Inform, Build), time-box, pre-read, log every decision with an owner and review date, and use meetings as leadership reps for staff.
    12	- **Module 4, The integration problem.** Sound technical work fails at five breakpoints (language, pathway, authority, relationship, process); structure the clinical to training grey zone with ownership, empowerment and communication rules; build dissent into the decision log.
    13	
    14	## Tools worth keeping
    15	
    16	| Tool | Where |
    17	| --- | --- |
    18	| Knowledge-Behaviour Matrix and Student Workbook | module-1 note; Lab_1b_Blog pp.1-3; Knowledge_Behaviour_Profile_Student_Workbook pp.1-5 |
    19	| Means, modality, technology ordering and the CM² athlete map | module-1 note; Lab_1A_Blog pp.1-3 |
    20	| Tech Stack Reality Check (inventory, reliability, one-page procedure) | module-1 note; Lab_1c_Tech_Stack_Audit pp.1-4 |
    21	| Measured, inferred, probability, next step communication | module-2 note; Lab_2a pp.3-4 |
    22	| Capability and Workflow Matrix | module-2 note; Lab_2b pp.2-3 |
    23	| Monitoring vs testing rule and the five coach questions | module-2 note; Lab_2c pp.1-2 |
    24	| Five-part decision gate and the MDC95 / SWC decision logic | module-2 note; Lab_2D pp.1-2; Lab_2E pp.1-2 |
    25	| Meeting typology cheat sheet, Kaigi, Stoplight slide, decision log, Lab 3D rep worksheet | module-3 note; Lab_3b cheat sheet pp.1-2; Lab_3a pp.1-3; Lab_3c template pp.1-2; Lab_3D_Worksheet pp.1-3 |
    26	| Grey Zone Workbook (people profile, operational logic, phase ownership, empowerment, communication) | module-4 note; The_Grey_Zone_Workbook pp.2-11 |
    27	| Six-check evidence stack and Bias Prompt Analysis | module-2 note; Stacking_Evidence pp.2-4; module-4 note; Structured_Thinking pp.6-7 |
    28	
    29	## Caveat on sources
    30	
    31	The lesson transcripts are unverified faster-whisper drafts with frequent mis-hearings. The PDFs are the authoritative source and are cited by page wherever a claim rests on them. Anything marked transcript-only in the module notes (the six-stage decision pathway, the Webinar 3 operating practices, the go/no-go run order, the 20-minute meeting rules) is the speaker's spoken account with no written backup. Course media and PDFs stay on Drive and are never committed here.

    78
